## Biography

Dr Rodrigo Gomez-Fell is a postdoctoral fellow at Gateway Antarctica,
University of Canterbury, in Christchurch, New Zealand. He uses synthetic aperture radar (SAR), a type of satellite radar that
works through cloud and darkness, to measure changes in glaciers, ice shelves
and sea ice.

His PhD in Antarctic Studies (University of Canterbury, 2023) focused on SAR
remote sensing and ice dynamics. His published work shows how the loss of
land-fast sea ice led to the collapse of the Parker Ice Tongue, how ocean
currents bend the Erebus Ice Tongue, and how ice tongues melt from below in
the western Ross Sea.
[TODO: thesis title and supervisors, if you want them listed]{.todo}

Before his PhD, he completed an MSc in Oceanography at the Universidade Federal
do Rio Grande in Brazil (2018), where he started using SAR to study
glaciers. His first degree is in Industrial Engineering from the Pontificia
Universidad Católica de Valparaíso, Chile (2006). He worked for more than ten
years in engineering and tourism, and then as a project manager at the CEQUA
research centre in Chile, before starting his MSc.

From 2023 to 2026 he was a Geospatial Research Scientist at the University of
Canterbury's Waterways Centre. There he developed national methods for mapping
New Zealand's braided rivers for the Ministry for the Environment, and estimated
forest carbon from airborne lidar for the Ministry for Primary Industries.

His current projects include calibrating and checking ESA's BIOMASS satellite
over Antarctic ice shelves, and using RADARSAT Constellation Mission data to
monitor end-of-summer snowlines on glaciers in the New Zealand Alps.

## Community

Rodrigo chairs the New Zealand chapter of the IEEE Geoscience and Remote
Sensing Society. He organised the first New Zealand SAR Workshop (2024) and the
second New Zealand Radar Remote Sensing School (2026), and has organised
sessions at IGARSS, the largest remote sensing conference. He co-supervises
research students working with satellite data.

## Research interests

- Antarctic ice shelves, ice tongues and their interaction with the ocean
- Land-fast sea ice and sea ice
- Ice flow, surface change and mass balance measured from space
- SAR methods: interferometry (InSAR), offset tracking and backscatter analysis
- Combining radar, lidar, multispectral and field data, including machine learning

## Education

- **2023** PhD, Antarctic Studies, University of Canterbury, New Zealand
- **2018** MSc, Oceanography, Universidade Federal do Rio Grande, Brazil
- **2006** Industrial Engineering, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso, Chile
